surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the adsorption of DMEAA on oxidized AI(111) surfaces, followed by decomposition into Me2EtN and AIH3. The AIH3 then dissociates into Al and H, while Me2EtN desorbs. The H atoms recombine to form H2, and the Al atoms react with the adsorbed Me2EtN to form AIN. The process is self-limiting and occurs in a stepwise manner with alternating DMEAA and NH3 exposures.
evidence: The surface reactions of DMEAA on AI(111) resemble that of structurally similar TMAA. The reactive sticking probability is very low at temperatures below 300 K and correlates with the number of surface defect sites. At higher substrate temperatures the reactive sticking probability is high and pure aluminum film growth is observed. The formation of AIN thin films with low carbon impurity levels is achieved in UHV using an ALG process at surface temperatures as low as 600 K. A DMEAA exposure on oxidized AI(111) at 600 K deposits a layer of aluminum that is subsequently nitrided to form AIN when NH3 is introduced in the following step.
